notes: Full assertion rationales live in each eval's eval_metadata.json in storm-research-workspace/iteration-N/. Mechanical checks (orphans, density, domain diversity, URL resolution) are automated by storm-research-workspace/check_citations.py.

evals.name: broad-topic-coverage
evals.prompt: Write me a proper article on the rise of 15-minute cities. I want it to actually cover the whole thing, not just the urban planning angle - it's become a political fight as well and I want to understand both. Save it somewhere I can read it.
evals.expected_output: A long-form article with a lead section, hierarchical outline-derived sections spanning at least urban planning, politics/backlash, and implementation evidence, inline [n] citations throughout, and a resolving reference list. Intermediate artefacts (perspectives, conversation log, outline) should exist on disk.
assertions: Research artefacts exist on disk separate from the article
At least 3 distinct named perspectives with substantively different questions
Hierarchical outline exists and the article's sections match it
Covers both urban-planning substance and political backlash, each with its own sources
Every top-level section contains at least one inline [n] citation
Citation density at least 1 marker per 150 words of body prose
No orphan markers or uncited reference entries in either direction
All reference URLs resolve when fetched
A citation audit artefact exists and reports a verdict
Reference list draws on at least 8 distinct domains

evals.name: contested-evidence-citations
evals.prompt: I need a well-sourced deep dive on whether creatine supplementation actually improves cognitive performance in healthy adults. There's a huge amount of hype on this and I can't tell what the evidence really says. Be honest about where the evidence is weak.
evals.expected_output: An article that distinguishes what trials/meta-analyses found from what is claimed, attributes findings to specific studies rather than asserting them, cites primary literature (PubMed-class sources, not just health-news write-ups), and explicitly states gaps and limitations. Every quantitative claim cited.
assertions: Research artefacts exist on disk separate from the article
At least 3 distinct named perspectives with substantively different questions
Cites primary literature (trials/meta-analyses), not only health-news write-ups
Findings attributed to specific studies rather than asserted as consensus
Hedging matches the sources: no 'associated with' rendered as 'improves'
Explicitly states where evidence is weak, absent or contested
Every quantitative claim carries a citation
No orphan markers or uncited reference entries in either direction
All reference URLs resolve and cited papers exist as described
A citation audit artefact exists and reports a verdict

evals.name: costorm-exploration-mode
evals.prompt: I'm trying to get my head around the debate over how AI diagnostic tools should be regulated, but honestly I don't know enough yet to know what questions I should be asking. Can you explore it with me from a few different expert angles rather than just handing me an essay?
evals.expected_output: Co-STORM mode: a warm-start research pass, named experts with distinct roles, grounded and cited conversational turns, a moderator intervention introducing an unexplored angle, a running mind map artefact, and pauses offering the user the floor rather than a 20-turn unattended transcript.
assertions: Co-STORM roundtable mode chosen over STORM article mode
A warm-start research pass happened before the conversation opened
At least 2 experts with distinct roles representing genuinely different interests
Expert turns are grounded and cited with [n] markers
A moderator intervention introduces an unexplored angle and is itself sourced
A hierarchical mind map artefact exists with source markers on entries
At least one pause point offers the user the floor
Every [n] resolves to a source entry and all source URLs resolve
Surfaces what is thin or contested rather than a smooth consensus
